newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel plans further broad spending cuts - magazine.
newsitem.headline: Waigel plans further broad spending cuts - magazine.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel plans further spending cuts in all ministries to achieve the three to four billion marks in savings needed for the 1997 budget, the news magazine Focus reported.

In an advance release of an article to be published next week, Focus said cuts in defence, transport and research spending were now a possibility. Waigel has previously said he saw little further room in those areas.
A Finance Ministry spokesman told Reuters that it had not yet been established what levels of savings were needed in which areas, but that all departments would have to contribute.
The issue will be considered in the run-up to the government's budget committee meeting on November 14, the spokesman said.

Germany aims to cut its budget deficit to 2.5 percent of total economic output in 1997, a comfortable margin below the three percent "reference value" demanded by the Maastricht Treaty for participation in Europe's single currency.
